name: Gum arabic (Acacia senegal)
short: Case report: a man had a systemic allergic reaction (throat tightness, breathlessness, near-fainting) to swallowed acacia gum. A heart-failure pilot trial found no safety or tolerability issues.
text: A 2026 case report describes a 37-year-old man with a 10-year history of episodic symptoms that resolved after he switched to a levothyroxine (thyroid hormone) preparation without acacia gum; a self-administered challenge with acacia gum caused throat tightness, breathlessness, tongue swelling and near-fainting within 15 minutes, and an oral challenge with 0.5 g of acacia gum reproduced similar symptoms. The authors note that hypersensitivity reactions to acacia gum had mainly been reported in occupational settings and that no allergic reactions from swallowing it had previously been documented. In a randomized pilot trial in 51 outpatients with heart failure, acacia gum fibre taken daily for 12 weeks (the abstract does not name the Acacia species) was compared with a non-fermentable fibre, and no safety, tolerability or adherence issues were observed. In a 12-week before-and-after study (no control group is described) in 47 patients aged 5 to 42 with sickle cell anaemia taking gum arabic daily, direct bilirubin and the liver enzyme ALT fell, aspartate transaminase did not change and urea fell only in the first month; the abstract does not report adverse events. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
